steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Two main types: Formal letters (to officials, businesses, newspapers) and Informal letters (to friends and family). The exam usually requires formal letters. | Salutations: Dear Mr/Mrs/Ms [Surname] - if you know the name Dear Sir/Madam - if you don't know the name To the Editor - for letters to newspapers | Sign-offs: "Yours sincerely" - if you used a name (Dear Mr Smith) "Yours faithfully" - if you used Dear Sir/Madam | Top Tip: In exams, you're almost always asked to write a formal letter. Avoid contractions and slang. Use sophisticated vocabulary appropriately.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: When should you use "Yours faithfully" versus "Yours sincerely"? | What is the correct order for a formal letter's components? | Write the opening of a letter to your local council about litter in your area.

steps.title: Homework & Consolidation
steps.body: Consolidation, retrieval on Two main types, Salutations, Sign-offs, and one past-paper question.
